_comment: The Browse surface's local seed data: one city, a week of events, and the two
accounts the walk-through signs in as.
The event times are RELATIVE — 'day 0', 'hour 19', 'minute 30' — and the command
resolves them against the moment it runs. An absolute date would put the whole
catalog in the past the day after it was written, and Browse's window is 'tonight
through seven days', so a stale file would seed an empty surface and the seed would
'day 0' is the local day of the run, in the city's zone. 'hour' is the local wall
clock. The command writes the UTC instant and the normalized 'start_time_local'
string, so the Event carries the same shape an ingested one would.
The titles carry the keywords deliberately: the chip matcher is a whole-word match
over 'shared.constants.INTEREST_CHIP_KEYWORDS', so a title only earns a why-tag if it
contains one of those words. The chip column below is the EXPECTED chip, and the
command checks the match against it — so this file cannot drift from the keyword
table without the seed failing loudly.
The 'reviewer' below is the person the seeded source's terms-of-service review is
attributed to. The ingestion services refuse a system actor for a review — a review
is a human saying 'I read the terms and they permit this' — so the seed signs it with
a named account rather than with the system. It is a fixture, like everything here.

tos.notes: A seed fixture. It serves no real feed and makes no network call.
